text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's President Aleksander Kwasniewski has signed a vetting bill to block the taking of public posts by former collaborators of the communist security police.
- Parliamentary elections will take place on September 21, Kwasniewski also said on Wednesday.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's current account deficit reached $2.3 billion in the first four months of 1997, showing 28 percent growth compared to the same period last year.
- The state treasury plans to boost social security funds with proceeds from the privatisation of 52 companies, the cabinet said.

- State-owned telecoms operator Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) abuses its monopolist position on the market through excessive fees for line leasing charged from private operators, the Competition and Consumer Protection Office (UOKK) said.
- The U.S.'s United Technologies Automotive Poland will invest $15 million in a new cable plant to be built in the Mielec special economic zone.
The plant will employ 1,200 workers, the firm said.
- Fiat Auto Poland will increase prices for most of its vehicles by three percent on July 1, 1997. Only prices of the Punto and Bravo/Brava models will remain unchanged.
- Japan's Sony consumer electronics maker is considering building a plant in Poland due to a growing demand for the concern's goods in the country and the huge nearby Russian market, Sony said.

- South Korean firms Daewoo and Rocket will buy a 75 percent stake in the Electron battery maker in Stargard Gdanski, northern Poland, for 136,000 zlotys, Stargard Gdanski's president Pawel Gluch said.
They will invest a further $8 million.
- Sales of the Plonsk confectionery plant controlled by the listed Wedel confectioner declined by 30 percent in February and March 1997 compared with forecasted levels.
The Plonsk plant accounts for 30 percent of Wedel's output.

- Last year's sales of the Inco Veritas household chemical maker were 290.6 million zlotys on a net profit of 18.3 million zlotys. This year the firm's sales will reach 332.1 million zlotys and net profit 20.9 million zlotys, the company said.
- Swiss Re Advisers reinsurance firm Poland will launch operations by the end of 1997.
Poland's rapid development makes it an important market for Swiss Re, company Central and Eastern Europe director Stephan Hirzel said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- The Levi Strauss Polska garment maker in Plock, central Poland, sold 12 million pairs of jeans in the last five years.
The plant now makes three million pairs of jeans each year, the company said.
- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and the Bank of America will invest $53 million in the Hortex vegetable and fruit processing group in the next two years.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poland and Russia will not start talks on a free trade agreement before 1999, deputy economy minister Jan Chaladaj said.
- A banking consortium led by Bank Zachodni will grant a 32.6 million credit to the Gdynia shipyard to finance construction of a container ship contracted by Britain's Ellerman Asia Ltd.
PARKIET
- France's Societe Generale will organise a $200 million credit cornsortium for the KGHM copper conglomerate, which will increase the group's turnover capital.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
